results.title: GUTA calls for cheaper credit, lower business costs in 2027 Budget
results.content: The Ghana Union of Traders Associations (GUTA) has urged the government to introduce measures in the 2027 Budget to create a more enabling business environment, improve access to affordable credit and support private-sector job creation. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse ahead of the budget presentation on Thursday, November 12, Vice President of GUTA Joseph Paddy said businesses needed practical support to expand production and create employment. He questioned what specific incentives the government was putting in place to help businesses secure cheaper financing and invest in manufacturing. “What is the government putting in place for us? So that when I go to the bank, I'll get cheaper credit, maybe a five-year moratorium to open a factory?” he asked.

results.title: Prepare to meet us in court – Rent Commissioner tells UGEL management
results.content: Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku has warned the management of the University of Ghana Enterprises Limited (UGEL) to prepare for possible legal action over its handling of accommodation fee increases at the University of Ghana. He says the Rent Control Department is considering legal action against UGEL for alleged non-compliance with the Rent Act, insisting that the department will no longer tolerate attempts by institutions to disregard its directives. Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem, Mr Opoku disclosed that he had cautioned the UGEL Chief Executive Officer during a meeting about the potential legal consequences of breaching the law, including a possible jail term. “At the meeting, I strongly warned the UGEL CEO that he risks going to jail because the Rent Act provides for a custodial sentence for certain breaches,” he said.

results.title: Kwadwo Sheldon hints at plans to contest Madina NPP parliamentary seat
results.content: Content creator Bernard Kwadwo Amoafo, famed Kwadwo Sheldon, has hinted at plans to contest the Madina Constituency parliamentary seat on the ticket of the New Patriotic Party (NPP). In a post on X, formerly Twitter, he highlighted his track record in entrepreneurship and job creation, saying his experience with building a media platform from limited resources had inspired his interest in giving back to the constituency. According to him, seven years ago, he and two other young men moved to Pantang in search of an apartment, where they eventually settled and began building their media business with laptops and mobile phones. He said the venture has since grown into one of the biggest media platforms in the country, creating employment opportunities for several people.

results.title: Mahama announces new offshore oil discovery in Deepwater Cape Three Points block
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has announced a new hydrocarbon discovery in the Deepwater Cape Three Points block in the Tano Basin, offshore Ghana. The discovery was made by Planet 1 Oil and Gas Limited in partnership with Bowler Upstream Limited and the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC), according to the President. Speaking at an event on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, Mr Mahama described the find as an important milestone for Ghana’s petroleum industry, noting that it marks the country’s first successful test of a Cenomanian-Turonian carbonate play as a primary exploration target. “The hydrocarbon discovery at the N1 GDA 9 1 X well in the Deepwater Cape Three Points contract area marks an important milestone for Ghana. It is the country's first successful test of a Cenomanian-Turonian carbonate play as a primary exploration target,” he said.

results.title: Ablekuma–Pokuase trotro drivers begin three-day demo over GPRTU charges
results.content: Trotro drivers plying the Ablekuma–Pokuase route have embarked on a three-day demonstration over what they describe as excessive increases in road charges allegedly imposed by the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU). The drivers say charges at various loading points along the route have increased from GH¢10 to GH¢15, while fees at some locations have also risen from GH¢15 to GH¢20. They have expressed dissatisfaction with the increments, insisting that the new charges are placing additional financial pressure on their operations. The demonstration follows reported confrontations at some loading points, where drivers allege that land guards attacked colleagues who resisted attempts to compel them to load passengers at certain bus stops. The drivers reportedly called the police following the confrontation, leading to the arrest of some individuals alleged to be land guards.
